description: c-saves: Rust-native world storage engine for Paper 26.3. CRS2 container: CSEC-v3/v4 section codec (v4 0xC8 adds a third flag byte: uniform light forms — all-0 BlockLight, all-0/all-1 SkyLight — collapsing the underground 2048-byte light arrays to flag bits) (compound palettes, vanilla 4-bit width clamp, frequency-canonical order, dense bit-packing), v0.6.0 SIZE: content-deterministic section RLE forms — the canonical voxel stream is additionally encoded as [idx u8][varint run] pairs in vanilla order (collapses horizontal strata planes) and in y-fast transposed order (collapses columns/vertical walls); the smallest of dense/RLE/RLE-transposed wins, so extreme-height JJThunder-style terrain sections collapse to a few dozen bytes while noisy sections keep the dense stream (dedup hashes stay content-pure), delta-varint heightmaps, per-key field split for entity/POI payloads, content-addressed section dedup with canonical permutation-invariant hashes, chunk-locality-ordered slab packing (mode-aware dictionary), id/varint recipes, versioned shared zstd dictionaries, hot/cold two-tier compression (hot=3: 2.1x faster writes at identical packed size) with auto-pack watermark, transparent Moonrise chunk-IO takeover, Anvil import/export. v0.5.0 SPEED: fused CSEC-to-NBT emitter, batched single-pass section loads, per-thread emit/encode caches, one-pass dense<->no-straddle converters, O(1) recipe-batch index, lock-free segment mmaps. 4 MiB section slabs (longer zstd windows). Real JJThunder corpus verified every push (bad=0 CI gate). v0.9.0: light-uniform codec + bigworld pack-drain fix (re-request pack per compact step — the old wave loop stopped after one segment and left 2 GB of z3 hot blobs unpacked) + streaming integrity scan with self-heal re-import + fixed palette attribution (fastnbt to_bytes needs a compound root; bare lists measured 0). v0.9.2 INTEGRITY: root-cause fix for silent chunk loss — gc_dicts deleted dictionary FILES that recipes' inline tails (Tail::Inline, tail < tail_blob_min) still referenced (blob-only accounting cannot see recipe references); dict files are now immutable (RAM map is a pure cache, decompress lazy-loads from disk, read->write self-deadlock in the reload path fixed), bigworld integrity scan gained per-key forensics (read_fail_reason names the first blocking stage) and a bounded-drain guard; regression test reproduces the loss via dead-ratio drop_seg compaction. v0.9.3: writer-segment ROLL fix - append() seeked to `written` instead of `written - buf.len()` while the append buffer still held unflushed records, zeroing the segment tail (batch recipes decoded rawlen=0, blobs decompressed to garbage) and the full-rewrite pack then dropped those blobs, dangling every recipe that referenced them (23,380 of 261,572 chunks unreadable on the 262k-chunk bigworld; JJ-corpus benches never roll a segment with a non-empty buffer, so they stayed clean). Roll now seeks to written - buf.len(); Cfg.seg_roll (CSAVES_SEG_ROLL); pack drop path is poison-guarded (unreadable victims keep the segment, never re-packed, loud logs); regression test forces non-empty-buffer rolls. v0.9.4: GLOB form ON by default - the 0xCB global state registry (jj_exp5 entropy winner, x2.16 on vanilla-terrain dense streams) is now the natural pack choice: sections convert to 1-byte global-id streams, slab stores whichever of canonical/glob compresses smaller, reads convert back to canonical CSEC. ROOT-CAUSE FIX for the former natural-choice corruption (JJ corpus verify bad=32): glob_to_section rebuilt target palettes in count-ASCENDING order while the canonical encoder is count-DESCENDING, so 0xC9 shift-ref members (which store their top planes as TARGET-CANONICAL palette indices computed at write time) decoded with rotated palettes against glob-rebuilt targets - andesite appeared at palette index 0, 32 chunks wrong. The rebuild now reproduces the exact enc_pal_data_canon rule (count DESC, ties (plain,name,props) ASC), making glob roundtrips byte-identical for encoder-produced sections; regression test glob_rebuild_keeps_shiftref_target_order fails on pre-fix code. New Store::slab_invariant_scan diagnostic cross-checks the blob map against on-disk slab entry tables; probe_glob/probe_bad2 examples document the hunt. CSAVES_GLOB=0 opts out. v0.9.5: GLOB2 (0xCC) forms — RLE-coded gid streams (vanilla-order and y-fast transposed, [gid][varint run] pairs) and u16 gid streams (registries up to 65536 states; modded worlds no longer fall out of GLOB at the old 256-state line — mid-conversion crossings switch the section's stream width instead of refusing), raw-u8 members keep the legacy 0xCB wire byte-for-byte. LATENT CORRUPTION FIX: the u8 unpack wrapped 9..16-bit voxel indices (palettes > 256 states) inside the canonical encoder's frequency counts + remap and the section identity — width-correct unpack paths everywhere now. The gform 2/5 payloads decode in transposed order and MUST un-transpose (the permutation is an involution); the first build shipped without it and the JJ corpus caught it as verify bad=2 (histogram-preserving permutation = the shift-ref signature). GID-RLE admission divisor (CSAVES_GID_RLE_DIV, default 8, 0=off): uncompressed-size RLE admission is the wrong gate for gid streams because slab wins come from CROSS-SECTION alignment — div=4 regressed the corpus to x2.99, div>=8 keeps x3.08 parity while keeping the lever for moderate-strata vanilla terrain. v0.9.6: hot-slab write batching - the import path stores a chunk's sections as ONE hot-tier slab frame (SLAB V2 wire + a new 0x40 hot-tier kind bit) instead of one zstd frame per section (~130 small calls per chunk were 16.5% of import wall time; the frame also hands zstd the whole-chunk window). Fresh members skip the GLOB variant on the write path - the cold re-pack re-decides the form with a 4-8 MiB window, so the drained container is identical to the individual-blob pipeline (corpus x3.07 verify 946/946 unchanged). scan() rebuilds 0x40 slabs as cold=false so pack re-groups them after reopen; pack-produced slabs now stamp cold=true (the slab flag alone used to gate re-packing). Import throughput +6-8% single-thread / +4-7% multi-thread on the real corpus, ensure-stage -36%; regression tests pin the batch roundtrip across reopen+drain and the below-threshold per-blob fallback. v0.9.24: the hot tier (write path) drops from zstd level 3 to fast level -3 - the pack pass re-compresses everything at the cold tier anyway, so the hot level only bounds transient disk usage and write-path CPU; import +13% (109-113 MB/s ST on the JJ corpus, 173 MB/s MT), ensure stage -37%, DRAINED container byte-identical across all levels tested (x3.36/x7.51/x4.01), verify 946+1280+728+218 bad=0, enc_fp pin unchanged. v0.9.25: parallel pack (slab compressions across cores; pack wall -21% local 2-core, expected -40-50% CI 4-core) + MT write hygiene (id_of guard hoist, supersede de-nest). v0.9.29: cold tier default z12 -> z6 (post-memo re-sweep: the palette memo made the build phase 4x cheaper, un-hiding compression - pack -43% at +3% container; every size gate byte-flat; below z6 the pack wall is the build phase again, so lower levels buy storage, not speed; CSAVES_COLD_LEVEL opt-out unchanged). v0.9.30: dict-training determinism - the sample pool was a frozen first-400-arrivals Vec (fs::read_dir order / spawn direction decided dictionary quality; a sandbox recycle flipped the JJ corpus between 1662 B and ~100 KB dicts), now a content-hash bucket reservoir: identical payloads collapse into one bucket, buckets keep their largest member, training iterates hash-ordered prefix (uniform w.r.t. content, arrival-independent, regression-tested byte-identical across arrival rotations); trainer input bounded to 32 hash-spread samples (35 ms, pack-wall parity with the old arrival pool); retrain gate on fresh coverage (>= dict_train/4) or +25% buckets kills version churn; cold tier is now dict-less matching the pack path (the shared dict earns its keep on hot-tier small writes; blobs carry their own dict_id so older dict-framed cold blobs decode as stored). v0.9.31: LOSS FIX - the writer thread's 192 KiB recipe-batch auto-flush could land a NEW batch recipe into a segment being compacted AFTER the packer's snapshot; the rewrite loop only iterated the snapshot, so the late recipe was never moved and the segment drop deleted its bytes (CI: 'chunk 19 lost after concurrent supersede+pack' at z6 timings). Fix: fixpoint re-snapshot - the move loop repeats until a full pass finds no recipe still pointing at the dying segment (terminates: after seal no new appends target it), poison escape prevents spin on mark_broken keys. Also: per-store write_skips counter (the global ST_WRITE_SKIP is shared process-wide and parallel tests bumped it mid-assert on CI). v0.9.32: split-path hygiene - the scan-split tail edit re-encoded every Heightmaps LongArray (9-bit unpack + roundtrip-pack validation + zigzag varint over 256 entries) on every chunk import; heightmaps repeat massively across chunks (flat regions, ocean floors, shared surface configs), so the dense form is now memoized per raw-array bytes (xxh3_128 key, thread-local, pure-function cache - identical input bytes yield identical dense bytes, enc_fp pin unchanged); the per-chunk feature env reads (KEEP_LIGHT/NO_SCAN/NO_SHIFT/NO_LITE) moved off the hot split path into once-resolved statics; documented negative: a byte-pair nibble unpack rewrite REGRESSED 2572->3228 ns/section (LLVM already vectorizes the constant-shift loop) and was reverted; the split-minus-scan stage delta (~58-68 us/chunk) is nested Instant::now() overhead on virtualized hosts, not work. v0.9.34: cold tier reverted z4 -> z6 by CI verdict - the JJThunder real-world corpora broke the ratio floors at z4 (survival x3.13 -> x2.50 vs floor 3.0, jj x2.86 -> x2.59 vs floor 2.6; the entire miss is region-stream cold level, entity bytes flat); z5 interpolates below the survival floor too, z6 is the fastest level clearing both gates with margin; the 3-stage GLOB split and parallel pack build stay (CI pack wall 0.19 s at z4, ~0.3 s expected at z6, still ~25x under 0.9.26); lesson: the cold level belongs to the real-world ratio gates, not to the GLOB-flat local speed corpus. v0.9.35: LOSS FIX - the supersede path eagerly removed the batch_idx entry BEFORE queueing the new pending recipe, leaving a window where chunks still pointed BATCHED at the old batch while batch_idx had no entry: every read of the chunk returned None (CI: "chunk 16 lost after concurrent supersede+pack") and a concurrent segment rewrite hit the batch_idx miss and poisoned the segment (8 misses, seg-2 KEPT on the CI run). Fix: the new pending entry is queued BEFORE the committed version's refs are dropped; the old version is resolved through the CAPTURED location via the new load_batched helper (immune to a concurrent flush re-pointing batch_idx); the batch_idx entry survives until the flush overwrites it; the segment rewrite gained a pending-skip (pre-pull + atomic check-and-push, anti-rollback) and an anti-spin poison when a stuck pending would never drain. Also: all 14 test env writes (std::env::set_var/remove_var) replaced with test-only override statics - the once-resolved GID_RLE_DIV/GLOB_DEBUG/FORCE_GLOB OnceLocks raced setenv from parallel tests (CI flake: glob-RLE form assertions failed on scheduling order; setenv concurrent with getenv is UB). Gates: 58/58 tests x8 runs at --test-threads=8, enc_fp EXACT (6d240d7166cdda99/12130/9971843), pack 0.41 s at z6 (2-core), container 1.94 MiB x6.42, verify 728+218 bad=0. v0.9.36: one walk, not two - scan_root now parses the section list IN PLACE at the sections key (parse_sections_direct_from, end-as-output; the raw skip_value pass over the chunk's bulk and the second walk in scan_split are gone; ScanOut::direct rides the parsed list out, refusal chain unchanged) - scanp 21.1us/chunk -> 0.03us, scan 222.8 -> 216.8, import ST 112.5 -> 114.8 MB/s; new root-branch probes (secb/hmap/skip) in split_stage_json decompose scan_root (hmap 0.07us post-memo, skips 2.3us); verdicts: enc-cache misses (12146/round) are the corpus's structurally unique sections, NOT capacity (flat at 32/256 MiB caps; 87% hit within one import) - the encode kernel (unp+pack 88us/chunk) is the next lever; container-fp documented as environment-drifted on this sandbox (4 values across identical-code runs), enc_fp stays the honest pin (EXACT, fused on and off).
